g_policy.reason: The offer is opt-in (the panel offers a game the reader chooses), the offer copy states the reward (30 minutes of unlocked articles), and the decline and failure paths are both defined. The lock itself is handled under g_no_free_removal.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes of unlocked reading, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event (the reader opens a fourth article today), and no chat content is involved.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The 'adds' field introduces a lock on articles after the third each day, which caps reading the model shows as free today (f01 Read a story). Article reading is not a resource that costs the app money per use, so the new cap is not allowed.

g_brand_safety.reason: The offer is a lock panel that an app event (the limit being hit) opens over s02 Article, which is rated safe. It is not placed in a chat or over unsafe content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: This is a product change, and the new resource is reading time in the article reader. The reader uses it for themselves in the observed core flow f01, and nothing goes to third parties.

c2_evidence.reason: 'What makes it work here' says flatly that 'The app has no paywall, limit, or currency.' The model only records that none was seen on the home feed (open question), so this is an unsupported fact about the whole app rather than wording like 'not seen'.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The product model shows no paid plan, so there are no paying users to spare.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 30 minutes and is capped at 2 per day. It gives away no paid benefit and takes nothing from other users or creators.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears at a moment of need, when a locked fourth article has just been tapped.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn sponsored game. The flow unlocks reading only once the play is confirmed, and the trigger (opening a fourth article) is an app event the app can detect.

c7_specific.reason: It names the home feed story card, the s02 Article reader, and the read-a-story core flow, and it builds on the article-open event.

other_concern: The idea rests on a newly invented daily article limit on free reading. Articles also already carry Taboola ads, so the lock adds a hard paywall-like friction to the app's core loop that may drive readers away.
